author: Mark Atwood
text:
[2026-05-11 recharacterize] Bead description and prior triage notes are misleading. Verified against actual code:

The trait `JmapBackend::query_objects` already accepts `filter: Option<&O::Filter>` and `sort: Option<&[O::Comparator]>` (see crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs query_objects signature). The bead's claim "Extend MailBackend::query_objects to accept filter and sort args" is incorrect — the trait shape is fine.

What the code actually shows: `handle_mailbox_query` at crate-jmap-mail-server/src/mailbox.rs:110 bypasses `query_objects` entirely and calls `backend.get_objects::<Mailbox>(&account_id, None, None)` at line 227-228, then parses filter/sort and filters/sorts in-process. The comment at line 224-226 acknowledges this is O(n).

Real scope (NOT a SemVer break):
1. Refactor `handle_mailbox_query` to call `backend.query_objects::<Mailbox>(account_id, filter.as_ref(), sort.as_deref(), limit, position)` after parsing args.
2. Implement `query_objects` for `Mailbox` in `MemoryBackend` to actually honor filter/sort (the reference impl can use a simple in-memory match; production impls would use indexed storage).
3. Update doc on `JmapBackend::query_objects` clarifying that production backends should honor filter/sort efficiently and not delegate to the handler.

Likely similar handler-side bypasses exist for other extension `query` handlers; audit during the fix.

Bundling decision (cancelled): does NOT need to ride the `g7wu.1` 0.2.0 mega-PR. This is a P3 quality-of-implementation refactor with no trait signature change. Can land standalone any time after `hwdv.5`/`hwdv.6`/`hwdv.7` (MemoryBackend extractions, all complete as of 2026-05-11).

Removing `human` label — this is a standalone refactor, not a design question.
